entry.name: crosspatch
entry.description: Connect a crosspatch to a client object (including matrix~, mcs.matrix~, mc.matrix~, matrix, gate~, mc.gate~, mcs.gate~, gate, selector, mc.selector~, mcs.selector~, and switch) to use a patching interface to edit connections between inputs and outputs.

attributes.name: allowdisabled
attributes.description: Sets whether connections can be made to disabled inputs or outputs.

attributes.name: annotation
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: bgcolor
attributes.description: Sets the object's background color.

attributes.name: candycane
attributes.description: Sets the number of colors to cycle through when displaying connections and labels. The default value of 1 shows only the; values above 1 show one or more of the candycane colors.

attributes.name: candymode
attributes.description: Controls whether inputs our output positions determine the color of a connection.

choices.digest: Input position will determine connection color
Output position will determine connection color

attributes.name: connectacrossdividers
attributes.description: Sets whether connections can cross any visual dividers (set via theattribute) that are currently showing.

attributes.name: dimmedconnectionalpha
attributes.description: Sets an alpha value to use for dimming patch lines not connected to the current input or output under the mouse cursor. A value of 0 would erase the lines completely, and a value of 1 (the default) would not perform any dimming. A suggested value ofto see the highlighting effect is 0.5.

attributes.name: dividercolor
attributes.description: Sets the color used to draw visual dividers.

attributes.name: dividers
attributes.description: To group inputs or outputs visually you can draw horizontal lines across theobject with theattribute. Dividers are defined using either the wordorfollowed by an index. The resulting vertical position of the line will bethe specified input or output. Note that divider lines are always horizontal so if the number of inputs and outputs is not equal, a divider defined by an input may cross an output or vice versa. You can prevent connections across the horizontal divider lines by enabling theattribute.

attributes.name: embed
attributes.description: Ifis true, connections are saved with the patcher and restored when reloading it. All attributes (including) are always saved with the object.

attributes.name: exclusive
attributes.description: Theattribute controls whether multiple connections from a single input or to a single output are permitted.

choices.digest: Multiple connections from the same input are prevented
Multiple connections to the same output are prevented
Multiple connections from the same inputmultiple connections to the same outlet are prevented.

attributes.description: Theattribute enables showing the numerical value of the gain control as it is changed.

attributes.name: gaindragmode
attributes.description: Sets how vertical mouse movement translates into changes in gain, particularly at the low end of the amplitude range.

choices.label: This setting maintains a constant relationship between the vertical mouse position when dragging and the amplitude value.

This setting increments or decrements the gain value by a proportion of the mouse position in dB when dragging. This mode provides slightly coarser resolution at the top end of the amplitude range and slightly finer resolution at the bottom of the amplitude range, which is more perceptually linear in most cases.

attributes.name: gainradius
attributes.description: Sets the size of the circle used for the connection gain control.

attributes.name: gainstyle
attributes.description: Sets the visual appearance of the circular gain control

choices.label: When theattribute is set to(0), a value of 1.0 is a 270-degree arc similar to the pie segement mode of the Max dial.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: , click on a white circle on either the input or output side of the object and either move or drag to the desired destination circle. The destination will highlight when the mouse is over it. If you released the mouse to start the connection, click again to complete the connection. If you dragged the mouse, release the button.click once on the line to select it, then press the delete or backspace key.To edit the gain of a connection, click on the line and drag upwards or downwards. A dial will indicates the current gain as you drag.As you edit connections with, any connected matrix objects will update to reflect changes in gain or connection state.

messages.name: bang
messages.description: Themessage will copy the current connection state to any objects connected to the left outlet. A dictionary with the current state is sent out the left outlet if any there are any connected objects that aren't compatible with theconnection protocol. Themessage sends a similar dictionary out the right outlet.

messages.name: clear
messages.description: Themessage clears all current connections and updates any connected clients.

messages.name: dictionary
messages.description: Whenreceives a dictionary containing connection information, it clears its existing connections and replaces them with those contained in the dictionary, updating connected clients. Connections for inputs or outputs greater than the current input and output size are ignored.

messages.name: dump
messages.description: Themessage outputs a dictionary out the right outlet containing the current connections.

messages.name: dumpconnections
messages.description: Themessage outputs a dictionary out the right outlet containing the current connections.

messages.name: indisable
messages.description: The word, followed by an input index starting at 0, visually disables the input if the second argument is non-zero and enables it if the second argument is 0. Example:will disable the second input, andwill re-enable it. When you disable an input, any connections to it will be removed ifis not enabled. Moreover, you cannot connect anything to a disabled input unlessis enabled. The disabled state of inputs issaved in the patcher.

messages.name: list
messages.description: A list of numbers adds or deletes a connection and updates connected clients. The first number is the input (always zero relative), the second number is the output (always zero relative), and the third number is a gain value. If the gain value is zero, the connection is removed, otherwise it is associated with the connection.

messages.name: outdisable
messages.description: The word, followed by an output index starting at 0, visually disables the input if the second argument is non-zero and enables it if the second argument is 0. Example:will disable the second output, andwill re-enable it. When you disable an output, any connections to it will be removed ifis not enabled. Moreover, you cannot connect anything to a disabled output unlessis enabled. The disabled state of outputs issaved in the patcher.

inlets.digest: list Adds or Deletes a Connection
inlets.description: You can update the state of theUI as well as any connected objects by sending messages similar to those supported by matrix objects.

outlets.digest: Connect to matrix~ or matrix Object
outlets.description: To allowcontrol a matrix object, connect this outlet to the left inlet of the target object.
